the_class_shared_folder: SECOND HALF, ruled separately in the same breath ('indeed so RULED') and kept out of now_the_spec_says only because the reading is capped at one line. EVERY CLASS SEGMENT IN THAT PATH IS A REAL FOLDER, AND A FOLDER CAN HOLD FILES. tools/<tool class>/ holds every instance of that class within one holder, so it can also hold files SHARED by them. Akien called it out explicitly to remove later ambiguity and bounded it in the same breath: 'i don't have a use for it in my head. but that use is not excluded.' So it is an AFFORDANCE OF THE SHAPE — permitted, deliberately NOT BUILT and NOT TICKETED. It is HOLDER-SCOPED: that folder sits under one device instance, so a file there is shared by that class's instances within that holder and by nothing else; there is no cross-device drawer for a tool class, and the absence is the point, because a tool's definition and defaults are the only thing that berths once, in class-space, in git. CC's observation, offered as such and not as Akien's word: the same physics runs at every class rung of the path — devices/<device class>/ holds all instances of the device class, machines/<machine class>/ all instances of the machine class — because the segment is a directory in each case. Nothing turns on this today; written down so the tool rung is not later read as a special case.
what_this_does_to_law_6: NOTHING — but it kills the REASONING that had been carrying it. Law 6 stands: a tool has USERS, not an owner. What is now wrong is the derivation 'a tool holds no state, THEREFORE it has nothing to gate'. The true version is narrower by one word: a tool has no state OF ITS OWN, because its ongoing state hangs off the HOLDER that assembled it and is therefore the holder's to own and gate. The test survives in refined form: anything called a tool that must gate writes AT ITS OWN ADDRESS is a machine.
the_sentence_that_dies: 'A tool holds no state' AS A PROPERTY OF TOOLHOOD. It is false. What is true is per-build and per-tool — 'TODAY this tool persists nothing' — and it is a fact about that build, never a fact about tools. Nothing is deleted from disk by this ruling, which is why what_dies is empty: the thing that dies is a sentence inside files that go on living, and every one of them is in what_conforms.
